scope: Mech compiler, runtime and language optimization studies; historical receipts remain authoritative.
hardware: Apple M3; each receipt specifies power, workers, source and timing conditions.
ratio_definition: speedup = before_seconds / after_seconds; elapsed_change_percent = 100 * (after_seconds / before_seconds - 1). These are within-study comparisons, not x-of-Mech language rankings.
rules: Append a dated entry after each optimization experiment; preserve failed attempts, old sources and raw samples.
Record source/compiler/library/policy changes separately; identify combined changes explicitly.
Require a measured matched cohort for a numeric effect; retain regressions and unchanged-object results.
Link raw receipts, source/compiler identity and a containing commit or frozen snapshot; a containing commit is not necessarily the exact implementation commit.

entries.inspiration: Scalar AOT backport from iros-workshop-benchmarks; SIMD/code-generation investigation against native submissions.
entries.mechanism: Lower fixed-shape ranges, gathers, combinations, reductions and updates to native loops; pack coordinates and preserve reduction order; expose FMA and algebraic powers explicitly.
limitations: Historical cohort: do not join its absolute times to later AC-power cohorts. FMA and algebraic powers change arithmetic policy. Refined reciprocal variants lost; no universal fast-math claim.
External scalar backport commit b10593b75ec8b9283ae33e4ac330c00dda9957d7 is a dependency provenance reference, not a Mech commit.

entries.mechanism: Prove bounded arithmetic and rounded comparison thresholds from source; replay a source-proved literal period; use a bounded two-buffer producer/mapper/output pipeline.
limitations: Counted Mech sources remain unchanged within each matched comparison. The final result combines several changes; most expanded arithmetic gain comes from bounded-index simplification. entries.title: Shared admission, JIT reuse and typed resident interpretation
entries.inspiration: General dependency/dispatch investigation; reusable coefficient batches rather than a cached matrix formula.
entries.mechanism: Share parsed documents between frontends, reparse only changed text, reuse admitted control IR, release parse storage; interpret independent coefficients in typed tiles of at most 32 independent elements/coefficient calls with whole-invocation unsigned proofs and checked fallback; inline count dispatch.
limitations: Three randomized rounds: 135 full-workload samples, 54 semantic checks and fifteen identical AOT objects. Fastest measured source is chosen independently per execution path; this is a combined change.
Resident timing begins after loading/activation; JIT uses whole fresh-process time including compilation. Do not compare these boundaries as a single pass. Resident fannkuch regressed 3.7%.

Before and after are separate completed cohorts with fresh AOT controls, not one randomized old/new paired batch. AOT control geometric-mean ratio was 0.999029530; that does not isolate each individual optimization.

entries.title: General count, bigint and regex operations
entries.inspiration: Reuse general Rust/native libraries as intended by Mech; packed-key and counting techniques compared with Rust/Julia/Chapel.
entries.mechanism: Optimize immutable dependency scheduling and packed extraction; use general counting containers and partitions, reusable GMP cells/direct quotient operations and generic byte-regex operations.
limitations: No isolated before/after speedup is asserted here without a matched receipt. The withdrawn eight-line k-nucleotide host shortcut was replaced by counted 17/24-line Mech bodies. The retained projects for the measured regex submissions pin regex 1.13.1. Rust regex::bytes supplies the general regex operations; the timing does not measure a Mech-generated regex engine.

limitations: Several source/execution variants were compared. A byte-identical native object for the equivalent row form does not establish a compiler speedup. Arrow mutation repair is a correctness fix; do not advertise an unmeasured runtime gain.

entries.title: Language gap repairs and pending algebraic floating point
entries.inspiration: General tuple/arrow/frame/bigint support; explicit floating-point policy investigation.
entries.mechanism: Add canonical form support and audit an explicit-f64 algebraic prototype on bounded semantic cases.

entries.title: Required-work correction and transitive scalar helpers
entries.inspiration: Inspect source-visible required work, rather than output equality alone.
entries.mechanism: Follow pure transitive scalar helper calls inside matrix comprehensions; reject impurity and recursion. Restore four spectral source functions and disable integer-cutoff FASTA transformation for the strict profile.
limitations: 51 native-sequence tests passed and 13 unchanged native compute objects remained identical. Corrected five-sample full medians are 0.088514667 seconds spectral, 1.227297416 seconds compact FASTA and 0.573187541 seconds expanded FASTA. These are new strict endpoints, not an isolated before/after optimization gain.

entries.title: Lane masks, recurrence organization and bounded FMA
entries.change_kind: source organization and compiler floating-point policy
entries.status: documented; no isolated timing asserted here
entries.inspiration: Eight-pixel grouping in Chapel submission #3; Rust submission #4 Boolean mask/integer arithmetic comparison.
entries.mechanism: Keep per-lane escape state in ordinary Mech source, group five recurrence steps per escape check, lower native masks and separate coordinate arithmetic from recurrence contraction.
limitations: Full FMA failed the complete official N=200 bitmap check and was rejected; recurrence-only contraction preserved the recorded output checks. Chapel #3 checks escape every recurrence; the five-step grouping is an explicit Mech source choice. Different source/grouping/worker forms have separate measurements; this entry makes no isolated-pass speedup claim.

entries.title: Share pi-digit extraction numerators in Mech source
entries.status: measured; admitted as separately retained source cohorts
entries.inspiration: The qualified Janet implementation forms 4*q+r by adding q to the preserved 3*q+r extraction numerator.
entries.mechanism: Reuse the mutable scratch bigint through existing general addition and floor-to-u64 operations, retaining both actual unbounded divisions. Inline the first extraction for a shorter source form. The same-sign quotient-only runtime path already existed.
limitations: Seven shuffled serial rounds; 35 complete full-size measurements across five exact implementations. The compact form is faster than its parent in all seven paired rounds.
All five subjects load the same installed GMP. Current Rust #3 is 0.309706 seconds (1.0677x optimized Mech AOT); Janet is 0.308255625 seconds (1.0627x). Historical medians are not pooled.
Mech and unchanged Rust retain the final generator state update; Janet omits it after the last digit. All perform 44,908 actual quotient divisions.

Physical rows 38 to 37, UTF-8 bytes 2050 to 2045, deterministic gzip 726 to 713, BPE tokens 715 to 713. These are complementary source measures; normalized and canonical formatted LOC are not claimed.
No universal fastest claim. Initial diagnostic interposer timed out and was reaped; corrected diagnostics are separate from all timed subjects.

entries.status: measured; admitted as separately retained runtime cohorts

limitations: Seven shuffled serial rounds; 35 complete outputs across five execution variants. Fresh whole processes include startup and all I/O.

All 61 parent/candidate input behaviors match; eleven existing broader FASTA source-contract differences are retained, not passed off as conformance. Official N=1000 and all full generated outputs pass.
Rust median is 0.109735416 seconds (0.8555x optimized Mech AOT). No universal fastest claim.
AC power, low power mode disabled; default power policy. Swap remains nonzero at 2025.12 MiB, with no temperature/frequency trace.
Native compute object is byte-identical. This is runtime input handling, not a new machine-code optimization. Trusted legacy I/O path; secure capability activation overhead is not newly measured.

entries.title: Reuse completed uniquely owned record storage
entries.change_kind: generic runtime allocation reuse; application and native compute object unchanged
entries.status: measured; admitted as separately retained runtime cohorts
entries.inspiration: Existing read/compute/write phase diagnostics and source-level allocation audit after record compaction.
entries.mechanism: After a mapped result has been written, reclaim only uniquely owned byte storage from completed values and formatting views. Retain at most one largest allocation in the streaming reader and grow it normally for subsequent records. Live aliases and captures remain untouched.
limitations: Seven shuffled serial rounds; all 35 full outputs and five official outputs pass. Same existing eleven extended FASTA source limitations, with all 61 parent/candidate behaviors identical.

Ten runtime tests pass; 2736 differential cases now recycle completed buffers. Test-only refinement rebuild is byte-identical to the measured executable. Initial rebuild refusal and corrected attempt retained.
Published Rust remains unchanged and takes 0.110701084 s (0.9010x new Mech AOT); no universal fastest claim.
Default AC power policy and low-power mode disabled; nonzero swap decreases by 24 MiB across the cohort. No temperature or frequency trace.
Whole-process startup and all I/O included; trusted legacy I/O, not a new secured activation comparison. At most one largest completed allocation can remain live until the stream closes.

entries.title: Reject four native text-output buffer policies
entries.change_kind: rejected runtime I/O policy experiment; production and application unchanged
entries.inspiration: Existing per-record phase diagnostics and the installed Rust BufWriter pass-through contract identified a duplicate output copy.
entries.mechanism: Test larger native formatting spans, then smaller outer stream buffers, while preserving application bytes and native compute object. Real generated-kernel pointer/call witnesses prove copy avoidance; full-process measurements reject every tested policy.
limitations: Both cohorts retain all samples; do not pool absolute times across them.
One original-parent run in cohort one has much higher RSS and elapsed time; it remains retained.
All four policies reduce median child user CPU slightly, but none improves median whole-process elapsed time. This does not isolate the cause.
Four-MiB policy has consistently higher child system CPU and observed RSS; allocation/I/O/scheduling causes are not proven.
Default AC power settings; low power mode disabled; nonzero swap; no temperature/frequency or allocation trace.
Eleven existing extended FASTA source-contract differences remain identical across each old/new comparison.
